'''Florentina Ioana Mosora''' or '''Florentina Stan-Mosora''' (7 January 1940{{snd}}2 February 1996) was a [[Romania]]n and Belgian [[Biophysics|biophysicist]]. In her earlier years, before 1964, she was a film actress in the [[Cinema of Romania|Romanian film industry]].

==Biography==
Mosora initially had a career in acting and was noted for her role in ''Dragoste la zero grade'' ("Love at Zero Degrees", 1964).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Crăciun, Cornel |title=Sportul în viziunea cinematografiei româneşti |journal=Studia Universitatis Petru Maior, Series Historia |volume=8 |pages=268–286 |year=2008 |url=http://www.upm.ro/cercetare/studia_historia/docs/studia8.pdf |access-date=2009-03-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091122190100/http://www.upm.ro/cercetare/studia_historia/docs/studia8.pdf |archive-date=November 22, 2009 }}</ref> She also starred in ''Sub cupola albastră'' ("Under the Blue Arch", 1962),<ref name="CITWF">{{cite web |url=http://www.citwf.com/person309481.htm |title=FLORENTINA MOSORA: Film Database - CITWF |access-date=2009-03-22}}</ref> ''Post-restant'' ("''[[Poste restante|Poste Restante]]''", 1961), and ''Băieţii noştri'' ("Our Boys", 1959).<ref name="CITWF"/><ref>{{IMDb name|0608875}}</ref> She was a graduate of the University of Bucharest's Faculty of Physics.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Florentina Ioana Mosora-Stan|language=en|oclc = 4779370905}}</ref> Later she moved to Belgium, where she worked on the use of stable isotopes in medicine.<ref name=pmid8889739/><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Lacroix | first1 = Marcel | last2 = Mosora | first2 = Florentina | last3 = Pontus | first3 = Micheline | last4 = Lefebvre | first4 = Pierre | last5 = Luyckx | first5 = Alfred | last6 = Lopez-Habib | first6 = Gabriel | year = 1973 | title = Glucose Naturally Labeled with Carbon-13: Use for Metabolic Studies in Man | journal = Science | volume = 181 | issue = 4098| pages = 445–446 | doi = 10.1126/science.181.4098.445 | pmid = 4718109 | bibcode = 1973Sci...181..445L | s2cid = 28672406 }}</ref> She was awarded the 1979-1981 Prix Agathon de Potter<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yQozAAAAIAAJ&q=Florentina+Mosora|title=Bulletins de la Classe des sciences: 1903-38|date=1982|publisher=Palais des Académies|language=fr}}</ref> for outstanding research work in physics by the Agathon de Potter Foundation and the [[The Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium|Belgian Royal Academy]].<ref name ="agathon">{{cite journal |title=Prix Agathon de Potter |journal=Bulletin de l' Académie Royale des Sciences, des Lettres et des Beaux Arts de Belgique. Classe des Sciences |volume=68 |pages=50 |year=1982 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yQozAAAAIAAJ&q=Florentina+Mosora |access-date=2009-03-21}}</ref> In 1989 she was one of three scientists co-organizing a [[NATO]] workshop on ''Biomechanical Transport Processes''.<ref name="Springer">{{cite journal |url=http://www.springerlink.com/content/t6763007pj525504/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130204171609/http://www.springerlink.com/content/t6763007pj525504/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-02-04 |title=Announcements |journal=Archive of Applied Mechanics |volume=58 |year=1988 |page=474 |access-date=2009-03-19}}</ref> She died aged 56 in Liège.<ref name=pmid8889739/><ref>Mosora, Fiorentina & Dauby, Patrick (1996) Stable isotope studies: a remarkable tool in delianating organic matter pathways between pelagic and benthic realms. In memoriam Fiorentina Mosora, ''Bulletin de la Société Royale des Sciences de Liège'', Volume :65, 9-13</ref>
